newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products narrowly mixed Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products narrowly mixed Friday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices turned narrowly mixed Friday amid bearish pressure from futures and fears of supply tightness.
Conventional grade gasolines edged higher as rumors of scaled-back crude use at refineries raised the specter of tighter supplies, traders said.
The possible production cuts come amid reports of lower regional gasoline inventories, which fell 835,000 barrels in PADD V for the ended May 16.
Tosco traders on Wednesday said poor refining margins forced them to begin cutting crude runs at San Francisco refineries earlier this week.
Traders declined to describe the extend of the cuts.
"Run cuts got the market jittery," said one California-based broker Friday."Everyone's spooked on gas.:

Except for Exxon's Benecia, Calif., plant, most Bay area refineries were rumored to trim their input of crude oil, as raw material costs continue to exceed the profits gasolines, diesel, and jet fuels earn.

Further pressure came from futures markets, where June deliveries of unleaded gasoline fell 0.01 cent a gallon to 66.92 cents, and heating oil eased 0.28 cents to 57.52 cents a gallon. Crude dropped 23 cents a barrel to $21.63.
++ DISTILLATES: June CARB diesel in L.A. rose 0.50 cents to 65/66 cents. Low sulphur diesel, or "EPA," grade eased 050 cents to 59/60 cents.

++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for June CARB unleaded gasoline at a slightly lower 63/64.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles. Reformulated (RFG) grade for sale in Phoenix, Ariz., was 1.50 cents under CARB.
Conventional grade stood 61/62 cents a gallon.
